metadata.title: Arbuscular mycorrhiza Symbiosis Induces a Major Transcriptional Reprogramming of the Potato SWEET Sugar Transporter Family

entities.name: mycorrhiza symbiosis
entities.description: Symbiotic interaction between potato roots and Rhizophagus irregularis associated with major transcriptional reprogramming of SWEET genes.

entities.name: major transcriptional reprogramming of the SWEET family in roots
entities.description: Extensive change in root SWEET gene expression during AM fungal colonization.

entities.name: arbuscule-containing cells
entities.description: Root cortical cells containing arbuscules that showed promoter activity for induced SWEET genes.

entities.name: root cortex
entities.description: Root tissue region where SWEET promoter activity was detected during mycorrhiza colonization.

entities.name: root tip
entities.description: Root tissue where some SWEET promoters were active under non-mycorrhizal conditions.

entities.name: sucrose
entities.description: Sugar discussed as being exported directly or cleaved in the apoplast during mycorrhizal symbiosis.

entities.name: glucose
entities.description: Sugar discussed as the main monosaccharide taken up by the fungus and as a product of sucrose cleavage.

entities.name: fructose
entities.description: Sugar mentioned as a product of sucrose cleavage and as a substrate transported across the tonoplast by clade IV SWEETs.

entities.name: RiMST2
entities.description: Fungal monosaccharide transporter from Rhizophagus irregularis that has the greatest affinity for glucose and is expressed in symbiosis.

entities.name: InvCD141
entities.description: Potato cell wall-bound invertase gene used as a symbiosis indicator and reported to increase upon fungal colonization.

relations.mechanism: Its promoter activity increased upon mycorrhiza colonization and was relocalized mainly to arbuscule-containing cells.
relations.evidence: The promoter of SWEET2c ... showed activity in non-colonized roots mainly at the root tip ... Upon fungal colonization, expression level was increased and relocalized mainly to arbuscule-containing cells.

relations.mechanism: Promoter activity was increased in arbuscule-containing cells during symbiosis.
relations.evidence: Promoter-reporter activity for SWEET7a ... symbiosis induces its expression and this is largely occurring in arbuscule-containing cells that show a much stronger GUS activity than non-colonized cortical cells.

relations.mechanism: Its transcript was induced and promoter activity became strong in arbuscule-containing cells.
relations.evidence: One of them is SWEET12a, whose transcript was induced at 8 wpi ... in mycorrhizal roots SWEET12a had a strong promoter activity in the cortex, particularly in arbuscule-containing cells.

relations.mechanism: Induced during symbiosis at 6 and 8 weeks post inoculation.
relations.evidence: SWEETs 1b and 7a ... were clearly induced during symbiosis at 6 and 8 wpi

relations.mechanism: Induced by Rhizophagus irregularis at both time-points analyzed and promoter activity was strongest in arbuscule-containing cells.
relations.evidence: SWEET7a was also expressed in control roots, and induced even further by R. irregularis at both time-points ... symbiosis induces its expression and this is largely occurring in arbuscule-containing cells.

relations.mechanism: The fungal monosaccharide transporter can transport several monosaccharides and has the greatest affinity for glucose.
relations.evidence: MST2 can transport several monosaccharides, including some pentoses, but it has the greatest affinity for glucose.

relations.mechanism: Expression of the potato cell wall-bound invertase increased when fungal colonization raised apoplastic sucrose.
relations.evidence: While StPT4, RiTEF, and RiMST2 were almost exclusively expressed in mycorrhizal samples as expected, the CW invertase showed also expression in non-colonized roots, although fungal colonization significantly raised its expression levels.

relations.mechanism: Colonization of potato roots by the AM fungus caused major transcriptional rewiring of the SWEET family in roots.
relations.evidence: Colonization of potato roots by the AM fungus Rhizophagus irregularis imposes major transcriptional rewiring of the SWEET family involving, only in roots, changes in 22 of the 35 members.
